meaning: Engulf weather reading: each day's forecast against past years, and what it means.
lead: 12 days away. Forecasts this far ahead are rough, so treat these as best guesses. This page updates twice a day.
banner: This is preliminary until about Nov 7, when the hour-by-hour forecast for burn night comes in. It gets more accurate the closer we get to the burn.
summary: Expect afternoons around 72°, nights around 52°, and a chance of a shower or two. Day: T-shirt. Night: fleece.
Burn night looks like light wind (around 6 mph), probably dry, and about 60° at the burns. Night: fleece.

A normal Engulf week: afternoons around 72°, nights around 45°. It rains on about 1 in 7 days, frost comes about 1 in 10 nights, and wind at burn time rarely reaches 15 mph. Day: T-shirt. Night: warm jacket, hat, gloves; winter layers in a cold year.
When you'll know more: the hour-by-hour forecast for burn night starts around Nov 7; from about Nov 11, three days out, forecasts are usually within a few degrees.
why: The latest forecasts from the European and US weather services make up 50% to 69% of each day's numbers. This far out they're rough, so the rest is what a normal Engulf week looks like, from 30 years of records.
NOAA's longer-range outlook leans slightly warmer than normal for Nov 8–14, so the normal-year part of Thursday and Friday and Saturday is nudged that way.
The last month ran warm and dry, but that says little about any single day two weeks from now, so it isn't in the numbers.
Each update leans more on the forecast; from a week out it's all forecast.
